items.stem: The inguinal canal is occupied by the spermatic cord in males and the round ligament of the uterus in females. Which one of the following statements regarding the inguinal canal is correct?
options: The floor of the inguinal canal consists of the transversalis fascia and conjoint tendon.
The posterior wall of the inguinal canal consists of the inguinal ligament and lacunar ligament.
The roof of the inguinal canal consists of the internal oblique and transversalis muscles.
The anterior wall of the inguinal ligament consists of the inguinal ligament.
Indirect inguinal hernias protrude through Hesselbach’s triangle.
items.answer_text: The roof of the inguinal canal consists of the internal oblique and transversalis muscles.
items.explanation: The inguinal canal is approximately 4 cm in length passing from the deep to the superficial inguinal ring. The floor of the inguinal canal consists of the inguinal ligament and lacunar ligament. The posterior wall of the inguinal canal consists of the transversalis fascia and conjoint tendon. The roof of the inguinal canal consists of the internal oblique and transversalis muscle.

items.stem: Which of the following muscles are supplied by the radial nerve?
items.explanation: The radial nerve (C5–T1) supplies the extensor muscles of the arm and forearm. Supinator, supplied by the radial nerve, is the main supinator of the hand when the elbow is fully extended, which inhibits any contribution from biceps brachii. Anconus, a small muscle supplied by the radial nerve, extends the elbow, helps stabilize the elbow joint and abducts the ulna during pronation. Brachioradialis, although a flexor, is supplied by the radial nerve.
